doc.headline: Keep {arm:September}: neither candidate holds Kairo in character better, and both cost more per reply to run.
doc.lede: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is clearly worse in character, down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points; {arm:1017} is not told apart from {arm:September} ({reading.1017.interval|interval}). Only a candidate that is cheaper, or measurably better in character, would change the answer.

caveats.material_if: Only if the judge marks the candidates' style down so that a real character gain is hidden. The keep call also rests on production cost, which no judge reads, so even then a candidate would have to be worth its higher cost.
Only if a different aspect should have been the question; production cost favours {arm:September} whatever aspect is read.
Only if a reference other than the production model was intended; both candidates cost more than {arm:September} and neither is ahead of it in character, whichever arm is called the control.
Only if a gap should be credited to the model alone: each candidate changes the served model together with whatever it brings, such as its reasoning budget. The keep call needs no such split.

decision.text: Keep {arm:September}, the production model, on Kairo. Neither candidate holds character better, and each costs more per 1,000 replies.
{arm:qwen3.8-flash}: clearly worse in character, down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points, and {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} dearer.

{arm:1017}: not told apart on the pass rate, down {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points on the judged holds-character rating, and {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} dearer.

The nearest margin: {weakest.arm} could lose up to {weakest.value|abs|pts} points of character against the {weakest.threshold|abs|int}-point allowance, {weakest.margin|abs|pts} points to spare; it does not bear on keeping {arm:September}. An earlier finding said {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production cost; here it costs more.

{arm:1017} spent {reasoning_ratio.1017|pct} of its output reasoning against {reasoning_ratio.September|pct} for {arm:September}, so its figures mix model and reasoning budget. Matching the reasoning would more likely raise its cost than lower it; its character figures could move either way.
Keep {arm:September} now. In parallel, reconcile the earlier cost finding for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and rework the off-lane directive, where most of each candidate's loss sits.

claims.text: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} passes character adherence less often than {arm:September}, down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points with its interval below zero; {arm:1017} is down {reading.1017.change|abs|pts} points, not told apart from it. Both drops fit inside the {aspects.character adherence (v2).margin|int}-point allowance. {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s rates leave out {scoreboard.qwen3.8-flash.lost|words} trials lost to harness failures, too few to move a gap this size.

evidence.caption: Change in character-adherence pass rate against {arm:September}, in points, at {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level}; the band is the allowed loss.

claims.text: Both candidates cost more per reply than {arm:September}: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} and {arm:1017} by {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k}, each interval clear of zero. The order holds even if every trial with no reported cost was free for the candidates and at its p95 for {arm:September}.

evidence.caption: Production cost gap against {arm:September}, per 1,000 replies, family-corrected at {family.level}.

claims.text: The judge's holds-character rating falls for both: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points and {arm:1017} by {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts}, each interval below zero. Keeping the booth offstage is not told apart from {arm:September} for either.

evidence.caption: Change against {arm:September} on two judged ratings, in points, family-corrected at {family.level}.

claims.text: Off-lane asks, {strata.off_lane.n_cases|int} cases, carry {strata.off_lane.loss_share.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character|pct} of {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s holds-character loss and {strata.off_lane.loss_share.1017.persona.holds_character|pct} of {arm:1017}'s: a lead found after the fact, not a confirmed result.

evidence.caption: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} less {arm:September} on holds character by kind of ask, in points, unpaired and uncorrected at {compare.qwen3.8-flash.September.persona.holds_character.strata.off_lane.level}; repeats are counted, so intervals may be narrow.

claims.text: Off-lane failures are not the candidates' alone: {arm:September} failed {count.failures.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|int} off-lane trials, against {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {count.failures.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane|int} for {arm:1017}. On the cards, {arm:1017} narrates the listener in the third person, {arm:qwen3.8-flash} gives advice on a landlord email it should brush off, and {arm:September} slips into a customer-service refusal.

evidence.caption: One off-lane failure per arm, from {count.examples.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words} kept per arm.

explore.control: The allowed loss in character adherence, declared after the results
explore.binds: Whether each candidate counts as acceptable on character
explore.outcome: Below {flip_margin.1017|abs|pts} points {arm:1017} is no longer shown within it, and below {flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts} points {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is not either. {arm:September} is kept at every allowance, because both candidates cost more.

omitted.why: It is the cost of running the evaluation, not of serving Kairo.

omitted.what: The delivery check (a Discord message or a queued voice line sent)
omitted.why: Neither candidate is told apart from the control; it does not change the call.

omitted.what: Failed-reply notices, tool provider faults, turns that ran over budget, items delivered
omitted.why: Operational counts with no separated difference that bears on character or cost.

omitted.what: The judge's overall outcome and transcript scores
omitted.why: Ordinal summaries of the same judging; they point the same way as the holds-character rating and add nothing to the call.

omitted.what: The other kinds of ask beyond the six shown, including story asks where one candidate keeps the booth offstage less often
omitted.why: Each has about ten cases or fewer, too few to read; all stay in the appendix tables.

omitted.what: A price per point of character
omitted.why: No candidate is cheaper than the control, so there is no trade to price.

next.text: Reconcile the earlier finding that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production cost with this run's production cost basis.
next.settles: Whether it is cheaper anywhere. If it is, the call becomes a trade between its cost and its character loss; if not, the earlier finding is retired.

next.text: Rework the off-lane directive and rerun all three arms on the off-lane asks.
next.settles: Whether the candidates' main loss closes, and whether {arm:September}'s own off-lane failures fall too.

next.text: Collect human ratings of holds-character, weighted to off-lane asks, to calibrate the judge.
next.settles: Whether the judged character losses are real or the judge's reading of style.

next.text: If {arm:1017} stays of interest, rerun it with reasoning matched to {arm:September} on {settle.passed.character adherence (v2).1017.September.cases_needed_80|int} cases per arm.
next.settles: Whether its pass-rate gap is the model's: at that size a run separates today's gap four times in five, if today's gap is true.

method.text: {cases|int} conversations, each run {repeats|words} times per arm. The corrected comparisons do not state whether their intervals count conversations or repeats; if repeats, they may be somewhat narrow.

The campaign does not state the rule that makes a trial pass; the pass rate is trials passed over usable trials. The judge's holds-character rating is a separate figure. The floor on character reads the pass rate for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and the holds-character rating for {arm:1017}; the two are shown apart, never merged.

Readings against the control are at {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level}. The {family.family_size|int} contrasts are corrected together by Holm's method, each interval at {family.level}. Breakdowns by kind of ask are unpaired, uncorrected and exploratory.
{judged.persona.holds_character.model}, with {judged.persona.holds_character.calibration_ratings|int} human calibration ratings; its calibration is insufficient.

Production cost replicates what serving Kairo costs, per 1,000 replies. Some trials report no cost: {cost.unreported.September.missing|int} for {arm:September}, {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.missing|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}, {cost.unreported.1017.missing|int} for {arm:1017}. Counted as free, the candidates would still cost {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.free|usd_per_1k} and {cost.unreported.1017.free|usd_per_1k}, above {arm:September} at {cost.unreported.September.at_p95|usd_per_1k} were its missing trials at its p95.
One setting, the served model, differs between arms; every gap is credited to it and to whatever it brings, such as its reasoning budget.
The asked aspect, the control, the allowed loss and the floor were all declared on {late_criteria.set_at}, the run date, after the results.
Latency, because every cell ran beside others; token counts and call counts, which were not reported; the simulated user's request settings, which were not recorded on every run.

findings.finding: This claim reads 1017 (B)'s holds-character contrast (-4.7, -8.2 to -1.3), which carries the reasoning-share confound: 1017 spent 55% of its output reasoning against September's 76%. Neither the claim nor the confidence line carries it. Add the reasoning-share caveat to the claim. A short clause would do: 1017's off-lane gap (-20.2) may partly reflect its smaller reasoning budget.

The claim rests on loss shares, 48% for qwen3.8-flash (A) and 53% for 1017 (B) (strata.off_lane.loss_share.*.persona.holds_character), but neither block shows them. Add the loss shares to the blocks, or restate the claim in terms of the off-lane gap the blocks draw. Also fix the caption 'overall and in each place both hold it': no overall row is drawn. Either add the overall gap (-6.0 and -4.7) as a reference row or drop 'overall'.

The lede says 1017 (B) 'is not told apart from September (P) (-5.8 to +1.1)', but that is the pass rate only. On the judged holds-character rating, 1017 is worse (-4.7, -8.2 to -1.3), and the declared floor for 1017 reads that rating. Say 'not told apart on the pass rate, though down 4.7 points on the judged holds-character rating', as the decision block does.

The Next line in the decision block says the off-lane asks are 'where most of each candidate's loss sits', but claim offlane gives 48% for qwen3.8-flash (A). That is under half. Say 'about half', and say it is the holds-character loss, not the pass-rate loss.

'September (P) failed 39 off-lane trials, against 64 and 62' counts holds-character failures. A reader may take them for pass-rate failures, which are 132, 200 and 159 overall. Name the rating in the sentence. Either add the counts to the block, or point to claim offlane's off-lane rates (65.8%, 42.9%, 45.6%) as their source.

The next step for 1017 (B) asks for '815 cases per arm', but the campaign has 299 cases, run three times each. Say whether 815 means distinct cases at three repeats (which needs 516 new cases) or trials, so the step can be costed.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, the decision block and claim character are enough to act on. They say to keep September (P), the production model. Neither candidate is ahead in character: qwen3.8-flash (A) is down 7.6 points, interval -10.8 to -3.4; 1017 (B) is down 3.0, interval -5.8 to +1.1. Both candidates also cost more. The main risks are named: the judge has no calibration ratings, and 1017's reasoning share differs from September's. options_dominance agrees, with September dominant and the call unchanged at every margin.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims build in order: character, then cost, then the judged ratings, then where the loss sits, then the example cards. I checked every block's rows against its sentence, and none contradicts it. Both cost intervals are clear of zero (+$0.38 to +$0.85 and +$0.17 to +$0.81). The missing-cost bound holds when recomputed: $2.24 and $2.36 for the candidates against $2.02 for September. One wording slip: 'most of each candidate's loss' in Next does not match claim offlane's 48% for qwen3.8-flash (A).

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The lede says 1017 (B) is 'not told apart from September (P)' without saying this is the pass rate. On the judged holds-character rating, 1017 is clearly worse: -4.7, interval -8.2 to -1.3. The declared floor for 1017 also reads that rating, at -7.1 to -1.7. The decision block corrects this, but the lede alone makes 1017 look like a tie on character. Next says 'most' of each candidate's loss is off-lane, but for qwen3.8-flash (A) the share is 48%.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: None of the omitted items would change the call. The call rests on production cost, and September is cheaper than both candidates with intervals clear of zero. Measuring spend is the cost of running the evaluation. The delivery check and the operational counts are not separated. A price per point of character has nothing to price, because no candidate is cheaper. The small kinds of ask stay in the appendix.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The model confound is carried in the confidence line and in Method, and the reasoning-share confound in a Watch line and a matched-reasoning rerun. Claims character, cost and judged also carry the reasoning-share confound. But claim offlane reads 1017 (B)'s holds-character contrast and does not carry that caveat, as the computed fact says. Its off-lane figure for 1017 (-20.2) could partly reflect the reasoning budget.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment and what it would settle. Reconciling the earlier cost finding would show whether this becomes a cost-versus-character trade. Rerunning off-lane asks with a reworked directive would show whether the main loss closes. Human ratings would show whether the judged losses are real. A matched-reasoning rerun of 1017 (B) would show whether the pass-rate gap belongs to the model. One small gap: the 815-case size for that rerun does not say how many repeats it assumes, or that 516 cases beyond today's 299 would be needed.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Blocks for claims character, cost and judged show their claims' own figures. Claim offlane's headline figures, the 48% and 53% loss shares, are not in its blocks: the blocks show per-kind gaps such as -22.9 and -20.2. Its captions also describe an 'overall' row that is not drawn. Claim cards cites 39, 64 and 62 off-lane failures, but its block shows only three example cards. It also does not say these are holds-character failures rather than pass-rate failures.
